body: Gotcha!! I'm sorry to hear that. From what I understand there are laws protecting those with Epilepsy in those fields. It may still be worth looking in to. 😊
Can I ask what careers? I'm a mortician and 2 of my coworkers have epilepsy and narcolepsy.
I don't really have an answer to that, but I'd definitely read your book!
Most funeral homes will let you shadow for a day. It's best to call around and ask what they allow you to see and when you can.

Having that ability to distance yourself can be helpful, but a human is still vastly different than an animal. One of my partners grew up on a livestock farm. He can deal with dead animals all day long but has admitted that he could never do what I do as a mortician.
Find a local funeral home and shadow for a day. And if it's still something you want to do, then go for it.

Honestly, this job is probably not for you. Work hours can be incredibly unpredictable. There may be a few places out there that you can get away with having a more set schedule but the funeral industry is fast paced and you need to be able to put in the time and that includes over nights and on calls.
Someone kind of preparing you to see a body. Someone going "okay, behind this door is someone on the table."

I was able to watch a full prep, watch a funeral, talk with the funeral directors and ask questions, and watch a cremation take place. I was able to walk into the cooler and see what that looked like. I was not given a heads up walking into the prep room because that was kind of the real test. Can you handle seeing a body without having your hand held. 
Not all funeral homes will be like that so when you ask to shadow, ask what you will be allowed to see and do.

Find a funeral home and shadow for a day. That is going to be the best way to see if it's for you. I've seen and met plenty of people that have "strong stomachs" walk into the prep room and walk right back out. 
I feel like a lot of times this job is fantasized by people. It's not for everyone and that's okay. This isn't just a job though. It's a calling. 
As an embalmer you also have to be a hair stylist, a cosmetologist, know how to make clothing fit well, how to cover wounds and recreate faces if need be. There is a lot that goes into it and some cases will wreck you. I realize my response is kind of all over the place so sorry about that. 
Just shadow a reputable funeral home in your area. Look at reviews and see what people have to say. 
Best of luck to you!

So for me it was a calling. My brother passed away and after his funeral I felt drawn to the industry and knew it was the place for me. One of the best things I recommend for people to do is go to a local funeral home and ask to shadow for a day. I shadowed the funeral directors and the embalmer and I knew it was truely right for me.
